verdict.rationale: Unleash documents a self-hosted Open Source distribution: you clone the repository and run it with Docker Compose, and community users recommend it as an open-source, self-hosted LaunchDarkly alternative. Self-hosting keeps flag data inside your own environment. However, the evidence shows the open-source build is not the full platform: RBAC, change requests, SSO and SCIM are tied to the hosted/Enterprise offering, custom roles are Enterprise-only, and the Edge layer that keeps targeting PII local is described as Enterprise Edge. Missing for 10: evidence that the full feature set (change requests, SSO, custom RBAC, Edge) ships in the open-source distribution, explicit docs on where open-source evaluation data resides, and hands-on corroboration of a production self-host.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can self-host the full flag platform from an open-source distribution, keeping evaluation data on my infrastructure

citations.quote: This guide helps you set up Unleash Open Source or Unleash Enterprise in your own environment using Docker.
To start the Unleash server, clone the Unleash repository and start the server with Docker Compose
user data (PII) used for targeting rules (like user IDs, emails, or IPs) is processed within the Edge node and never sent to the Unleash Cloud or your upstream instance
